advanced-communications-and-networks--ps.title: 4-stage LFSR producing an m-sequence
lines: uint8_t lfsr = 0x1;                    /* never the all-zero state */
advanced-communications-and-networks--ps.note: With the right taps the register visits all 2^4 - 1 non-zero states before repeating, one chip per shift.

advanced-communications-and-networks--wa.title: 4 x 4 Hadamard rows as spreading codes
advanced-communications-and-networks--wa.note: Any two rows agree in exactly half the chips, so W1 dot W2 = 1 - 1 - 1 + 1 = 0: the set is orthogonal.

advanced-communications-and-networks--co.title: two CDMA users on one chip stream
advanced-communications-and-networks--co.note: Each receiver correlates the shared stream with its own code; the other code is orthogonal, so it sums to zero.

advanced-communications-and-networks--so.title: soft handoff: make before break

steps.label: allocate a traffic channel in the target cell
second leg established, both cells serve
old pilot below T_DROP: drop the leg

advanced-communications-and-networks--so.note: Both legs carry the same frame during the overlap, so the mobile never breaks the link before the new one works.

advanced-communications-and-networks--re.title: Mobile IP registration through a foreign agent

steps.label: forward the request with the FA address
authenticate, bind home address to CoA
registration reply with lifetime and code
relay the reply to the mobile node

advanced-communications-and-networks--re.note: Until the binding exists the home agent still tunnels to the old care-of address, so registration precedes the move.

advanced-communications-and-networks--tu.title: Mobile IP encapsulation overhead
rows: short forwarding header: src, dst, protocol, checksum
outer IP header plus a GRE header
the original datagram is routed unchanged
advanced-communications-and-networks--tu.note: Every added byte lowers the effective MTU of the tunnel, which is why minimal encapsulation exists for small links.

advanced-communications-and-networks--wi.title: WAP stack and its WWW counterpart
rows: content and presentation on a small screen
encryption and authentication on the air link
GSM, GPRS, CDMA, SMS and other carriers
advanced-communications-and-networks--wi.note: Each WWW layer is replaced by a version tuned for narrowband links; a gateway translates to HTTP at the carrier.

advanced-communications-and-networks--cy.title: cyclic prefix cost in an OFDM symbol
advanced-communications-and-networks--cy.note: The guard interval must exceed the delay spread; lengthening it removes ISI but spends more of each symbol on redundant data.

advanced-communications-and-networks--pa.title: PAPR of N equal-amplitude subcarriers
advanced-communications-and-networks--pa.note: Since the worst case is every subcarrier adding in phase, the amplifier must back off about 18 dB or the peaks clip.

advanced-communications-and-networks--sp.title: capacity of a 4 x 4 spatial multiplexing link
advanced-communications-and-networks--sp.note: Each antenna pair adds one independent stream, so capacity grows linearly with min(Nt, Nr) and only logarithmically with SNR.

advanced-communications-and-networks--ie.title: IEEE 802.11 amendments at a glance
advanced-communications-and-networks--ie.note: Each amendment buys rate from wider channels, denser modulation or more spatial streams, never from a new medium.

advanced-communications-and-networks--mm.title: LTE core elements and their planes
rows: radio link, scheduling, ciphering, header compression
NAS signalling, paging, bearer setup, authentication
anchors user packets between eNodeB and P-GW
allocates the UE address, links to external networks
subscriber database that feeds the MME
advanced-communications-and-networks--mm.note: LTE separates the planes: the MME never touches a user packet, and the gateways never terminate signalling.
